tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Global boundedness] 1. ch8:8.15\group ch08-generalized-solutions Assume (8.5), (8.6), $f^i\in L^q(\Omega )$, and $g\in L^{q/2}(\Omega )$ for some $q>n$. If $u\in W^{1,2}(\Omega )$ is a subsolution with $u\leq 0$ on $\partial \Omega $, then \begin{equation} \sup _\Omega u\leq C(\| u^+\| _2+k), \qquad k=\lambda ^{-1}(\| f\| _q+\| g\| _{q/2}), \tag {8.34} \end{equation} where $C=C(n,\nu ,q,|\Omega |)$. The corresponding supersolution estimate follows by replacing $u$ with $-u$.
Proof

\sketch Put $w=u^++k$ and, for a truncated power $H$, test with

\begin{equation} \tag {8.35} v=G(w)=\int _k^w|H'(s)|^2\, ds. \end{equation}

The structural inequalities and Sobolev’s inequality give

\begin{equation} \tag {8.36} \| H(w)\| _{2\widehat n/(\widehat n-2)} \leq C\| wH'(w)\| _{2q/(q-2)}. \end{equation}

After removing the truncation,

\begin{equation} \tag {8.37} \| w\| _{\beta \chi q^*}\leq (C\beta )^{1/\beta }\| w\| _{\beta q^*}, \qquad q^*=\frac{2q}{q-2},\quad \chi >1. \end{equation}

Iterate with $\beta =\chi ^m$, pass to $L^\infty $, and interpolate down to $L^2$.

□
